title: The Phases of Matter
label: fig:ch01:s01:f01
caption: Ice and liquid water in glasses, a glass of water, and a steaming kettle illustrate the solid, liquid, and gas phases of water. Water vapor itself is invisible; the visible mist near a kettle consists of tiny liquid droplets.

assets.credit: Cleiton Andrade Andrade from Alfenas, Brasil
assets.alt: Ice cubes floating in liquid water in drinking glasses.
assets.title: Ice cubes on water

assets.title: Glass of water

assets.alt: A kettle emitting a visible cloud of condensed water droplets.
assets.title: Steaming Kettle - Boston, MA

title: Chemical Properties
label: fig:ch01:s01:f02
caption: A burning match demonstrates a chemical property: the match material reacts with oxygen to form new substances.

assets.alt: A wooden match burning with a bright flame.
assets.title: Burning matchstick 2010
assets.changes: Resized and optimized for the web; no content changes.

title: Physical Changes
label: fig:ch01:s01:f03
caption: An ice cube melts on a sunlit stone. Melting changes water from a solid to a liquid without changing its chemical composition.

assets.alt: A small melting ice cube on a stone, with water running onto the pavement.
assets.title: Eiswürfel auf Stein
assets.changes: Resized and optimized for the web; no content changes.

title: Types of Mixtures
label: fig:ch01:s01:f04
caption: The nuts and dried fruit in trail mix remain visibly distinct, making it a heterogeneous mixture. In contrast, salt dissolved in water forms a uniform solution. Such a solution looks like the glass of water shown below; the dissolved salt would not be visible.

assets.alt: A mixture of nuts and dried fruit with visibly different components.
assets.title: Studentenfutter 01
assets.changes: Resized and optimized for the web; no content changes.

assets.alt: A glass of water illustrating the uniform appearance of a solution.
assets.title: Glass of water
assets.changes: Resized and optimized for the web; no content changes.

title: Semimetals
label: fig:ch01:s01:f05
caption: Silicon is a metalloid: it has a metallic luster but is brittle, and its electrical conductivity is intermediate between that of typical metals and nonmetals.

assets.alt: A shiny, irregular piece of crystalline silicon.
assets.title: SiliconCroda
assets.changes: Resized and optimized for the web; no content changes.

title: Defining a Law
label: fig:ch01:s02:f01
caption: A speed limit is a rule made by people and can be broken. A scientific law instead describes a regularity observed in nature.

assets.commons_title: File:Speed Limit 20 sign on Commercial Drive, Southbridge, Massachusetts.jpg
assets.alt: A roadside sign specifying a speed limit of 20 miles per hour.
assets.title: Speed Limit 20 sign on Commercial Drive, Southbridge, Massachusetts
assets.changes: Resized and optimized for the web; no content changes.

title: Using Scientific Notation
label: fig:ch02:s01:f01
caption: A calculator displays a number as a coefficient multiplied by a power of ten. This notation avoids writing a long string of zeros.

assets.alt: A calculator display showing 9.7965837 multiplied by ten to the negative fifth power.
assets.title: Scientific notation in calculator display 16
assets.changes: Resized and optimized for the web; no content changes.

title: Scientific Notation on a Calculator
label: fig:ch02:s01:f02
caption: Scientific calculators provide keys for entering powers of ten. The key sequence varies by model; consult the instructions for the calculator you use.

assets.alt: A Casio fx-991EX scientific calculator with a multiplication-by-ten-to-a-power key.
assets.title: Casio fx-991EX Scientific Calculator
assets.changes: Resized and optimized for the web; no content changes.

title: Significant Figures
label: fig:ch02:s03:f05
caption: This odometer reads 173386.2 miles, reporting distance to the nearest tenth of a mile. The last displayed digit indicates the resolution of the measurement; adding further digits would imply unsupported precision.

assets.alt: A digital automobile odometer reading 173386.2 miles.
assets.title: Digital odometer 1987 Oldsmobile Toronado
assets.changes: Resized and optimized for the web; no content changes.

title: NaCl = Table Salt
label: fig:ch03:s04:f01
caption: A close-up of a table-salt crystal. Sodium chloride is an ionic compound with equal numbers of sodium ions and chloride ions, represented by the formula NaCl.

assets.alt: A magnified sodium chloride crystal with angular surface features.
assets.title: Table Salt (NaCl) Crystal
assets.changes: Resized and optimized for the web; no content changes.

title: Calories on Food Labels
label: fig:ch07:s01:f01
caption: An FDA example nutrition label lists 230 Calories per serving. In food labeling, a Calorie is a kilocalorie: 1 Cal = 1 kcal = 4,184 J.

assets.alt: An FDA Nutrition Facts label showing 230 Calories per serving.
assets.title: FDA Nutrition Facts Label 2016
assets.changes: Resized and optimized for the web; no content changes.

title: Liquids and Gravity
label: fig:ch10:s02:f01
caption: A water sphere floats beside an astronaut’s fingers aboard the International Space Station. In microgravity, surface tension draws the water into a nearly spherical shape instead of allowing it to settle at the bottom of a container.

assets.commons_title: File:Iss072e069743 (Oct 19, 2024) --- The fingers of NASA astronaut and Expedition 72 Flight Engineer Don Pettit are refracted in this sphere of water in the microgravity environment of the International Space Station.jpg
assets.alt: An astronaut’s fingers next to a floating sphere of water inside the International Space Station.
assets.title: Water sphere aboard the International Space Station
assets.changes: Resized and optimized for the web; no content changes.

title: Effects of Surface Tension
label: fig:ch10:s03:f06
caption: Surface tension helps water form rounded droplets on a leaf. The interaction between the water and the leaf surface also affects the droplets’ shape.

assets.alt: Rounded water droplets resting on green leaves.
assets.title: Water droplets leaf
assets.changes: Resized and optimized for the web; no content changes.

title: Walking on Water
label: fig:ch10:s03:f07
caption: A water strider rests on the surface of a river. Its water-repellent legs spread its weight, and surface tension supports it without breaking the surface.

assets.alt: A water strider on clear water, with dimples beneath its legs and shadows on the riverbed.
assets.title: Water strider on Natisone river
assets.changes: Resized and optimized for the web; no content changes.

title: Concentration in Commercial Applications
label: fig:ch11:s02:f01
caption: A commercial hydrogen peroxide bottle states a concentration of 3%. Concentration labels specify how much solute is present in a solution; the convention used for a percentage should always be checked.

assets.alt: A brown hydrogen peroxide bottle labeled solution 3%.
assets.title: Hydrogen Peroxide Bottle
assets.changes: Resized and optimized for the web; no content changes.

title: Salt and Safety
label: fig:ch11:s05:f01
caption: Trucks stand in a road-salt storage facility. Salt spread on icy roads dissolves in water and lowers the freezing point of the resulting solution.

assets.alt: Road-salt trucks inside a storage building containing piles of salt.
assets.title: RoadSaltTrucks
assets.changes: Resized and optimized for the web; no content changes.

title: Button Batteries
label: fig:ch14:s03:f03
caption: Button cells supply electrical energy to small electronic devices. Their compact form comes in several sizes and chemistries.

assets.alt: Several round button-cell batteries of different diameters.
assets.title: Coin-cells
assets.changes: Resized and optimized for the web; no content changes.

title: Lead Storage Batteries
label: fig:ch14:s03:f04
caption: A cutaway view of an automotive lead-acid battery shows its positive and negative plates, separators, and connections. Multiple cells connected in series provide the voltage needed to start an engine.

assets.credit: National Institute of Standards and Technology Digital Collections, Gaithersburg, MD 20899

title: Detecting Radioactivity
label: fig:ch15:s03:f01
caption: A Geiger counter and its connected probe detect ionizing radiation. Radiation entering the detector produces electrical pulses that can be displayed or heard as clicks.

assets.alt: A portable Geiger counter with a meter and a connected detector probe.
assets.title: Geiger counter 2
assets.changes: Resized and optimized for the web; no content changes.

title: Three-Dimensional Representation of Methane
label: fig:ch16:s01:f01
caption: In methane, the carbon atom (dark sphere) bonds to four hydrogen atoms (light spheres). The bonds point toward the corners of a tetrahedron rather than lying in one plane.

assets.alt: A ball-and-stick model of methane with four hydrogen atoms arranged tetrahedrally around carbon.
assets.title: Methane-3D-balls
assets.changes: Resized and optimized for the web; no content changes.

title: Combustion
label: fig:ch16:s01:f02
caption: A gas stove burns hydrocarbon fuel in oxygen and releases heat. Complete combustion produces carbon dioxide and water.

assets.alt: Blue flames and a few yellow tips surrounding a gas-stove burner.
assets.title: Gas stove burner flame
assets.changes: Resized and optimized for the web; no content changes.

title: Nucleotides
label: fig:ch16:s06:f02
caption: A nucleotide contains a nitrogen-containing base, a five-carbon sugar, and one or more phosphate groups. The diagram distinguishes the sugar-base nucleoside from its mono-, di-, and triphosphate nucleotides. DNA and RNA chains contain nucleotide residues linked through phosphate groups.

assets.alt: Diagram labeling the base, pentose sugar, and phosphate groups of a nucleotide; ribose has OH at the 2-prime position and deoxyribose has H.
assets.title: Nucleotide nucleoside general
